mainTopic: Whether רבי שמעון's view of a stingy consecrator fits a ברייתא about redeeming trees and land, and רב הונא's rulings on items with two legal statuses.
overview: Just before this, the גמרא said a ברייתא about consecrated trees follows רבי שמעון, who holds that one who consecrates does so stingily (בעין רעה). The amud first answers a problem: רבי שמעון's reason 'since they draw from a consecrated field' sounds generous. The answer is that he was only arguing on the רבנן's terms. Next the גמרא challenges the end of that ברייתא. It brings a ברייתא about a son who bought a field from his father, which seems to show that רבי שמעון goes by the time of redemption. If so, the trees should be redeemed together with their land. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that in general רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון do not go by the time of פדיון. Their ruling comes from the wording of the פסוק. Then רב הונא teaches that a grafted carob and a sycamore trunk have the status of both a tree and land. He also teaches that a sheaf of two סאה counts as both a sheaf and a heap for the laws of שכחה. Finally, ריש לקיש says that whether these two trees become הקדש with a field depends on the argument between רבי מנחם בר יוסי and the רבנן.

steps.title: The difficulty from רבי שמעון's own reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is still a problem: רבי שמעון himself gave the reason 'since they draw from a consecrated field,' which sounds like a generous consecrator.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still difficult, because רבי שמעון said the carob and sycamore are consecrated 'since they draw nourishment from a consecrated field'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up a problem. If רבי שמעון holds that a consecrator gives stingily, why did he himself say some trees are consecrated because they feed from the הקדש field?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stingy consecrator would keep land around the trees for himself, so those trees would not draw from הקדש land at all. רבי שמעון's reason assumes the land under the trees was consecrated. That looks like the generous view (בעין יפה), which seems to contradict what was just said about him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a problem that has not been solved yet
Since; because
They draw nourishment (literally, they suck)
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: But it is difficult:
"since they draw nourishment from a consecrated field"!
phrases.notes: This quotes רבי שמעון's own reason. It assumes the ground under the trees became הקדש too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the open contradiction carried over from the discussion before this passage.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון holds מקדיש בעין רעה מקדיש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reason 'they draw from a consecrated field' only works if the land around the trees was consecrated. That is generous consecrating.

steps.title: רבי שמעון was arguing on the Rabbis' terms
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון really holds that a consecrator is stingy. His statement about the carob and sycamore was only said to the Rabbis according to their own view. The Rabbis answered that there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי שמעון was speaking to the Rabbis using their own view. He said: 'In my view, just as a seller sells stingily, a consecrator also consecrates stingily and keeps some land for himself. In your view, at least agree with me that he consecrated only the grafted carob and the sycamore trunk!' And the Rabbis told him: there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem. רבי שמעון's 'since they draw from הקדש' line was not his own opinion. It was an argument he made using the Rabbis' opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his own view, a consecrator keeps land for himself, so not even the carob and sycamore are consecrated. He only told the Rabbis: even if you hold the consecrator is generous, at least limit it to these two trees, which feed from the הקדש ground. The Rabbis refused, saying everything in the field is included.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their words; arguing from the other side's view
With a stingy eye; giving as little as possible
He keeps back a part for himself
A grafted carob tree
The trunk of a sycamore tree
There is no difference

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון holds that one who consecrates does so stingily (בעין רעה), just like a seller. His statement about the carob and sycamore was only an argument made on the Rabbis' terms.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי שמעון's words in the משנה as his own opinion. He is saying 'even by your view, at least agree with me on this much.'

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Shimon
was speaking to them according to the words of the Rabbis:
According to me, just as one who sells
sells with a stingy eye,
one who consecrates also consecrates with a stingy eye
and he keeps something back for himself;
according to you, at least agree with me
that he consecrated only
the grafted carob and the sycamore trunk!
And the Rabbis said to him: There is no difference.
phrases.notes: The Rabbis mean that everything in the field is consecrated, not just these two trees.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a statement as said on the other side's terms (לדבריהם)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's reason 'they draw from הקדש' showed his own view that a consecrator is generous.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only arguing within the Rabbis' view. In his own view a consecrator is stingy and keeps land for himself.

steps.title: Quoting the end of the ברייתא about trees and land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא it said follows רבי שמעון and quotes its last clause: trees consecrated first and land consecrated later are redeemed separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom did you explain the ברייתא? According to רבי שמעון? Say the last clause: 'And moreover, even if he consecrated the trees and afterward consecrated the land, when he redeems, he redeems the trees at their value, and then redeems the land at fifty silver shekels for each area sown with a חומר of barley.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It quotes the end of the ברייתא so it can show in the next step that this clause does not fit רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this clause the trees and land were consecrated one after the other, so each one is redeemed on its own terms. The trees are redeemed at their market value, and the land at the fixed price set by the תורה. The question is whether רבי שמעון would agree to this split.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you establish (explain) it?
Say the last clause
Redeems; buys back from הקדש
At their actual value
An area that takes a חומר of barley seed to sow

phrases.english: In accordance with whom did you establish it?
In accordance with Rabbi Shimon?
Say the last clause:
And not only that, but even
if he consecrated the trees
and afterward consecrated the land,
when he redeems,
he redeems the trees at their value,

phrases.aramaic: וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים
phrases.english: and then redeems an area for sowing a ḥomer of barley
for fifty silver shekels.
phrases.notes: This is the fixed redemption price for a field, from ויקרא 27:16.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתָּא לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי שמעון contradiction behind and opens a new challenge from the ending of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier claim that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: it brings the last clause, whose ruling will be shown in the next step to clash with רבי שמעון's approach.

steps.title: רבי שמעון goes by the time of redemption
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, the trees should be redeemed together with the land. He goes by the time of redemption, and by then both are הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is רבי שמעון, he should go by the time of redemption, and the trees should be redeemed along with their land. After all, we have heard that רבי שמעון goes by the time of redemption!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes its challenge. Since רבי שמעון judges things by how they stand at the moment of redemption, the trees should not be redeemed separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment of redemption, both the trees and the land belong to הקדש. By רבי שמעון's rule, the trees should simply be part of the field and covered by the fixed fifty-shekel price. The ברייתא redeems the trees separately at their value, which seems to contradict רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him go after; follow
Redemption
Along with their land
We have heard him (say elsewhere)

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge puts the whole claim that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון in doubt. The sugya now has to explain how the end of the ברייתא fits him.

phrases.english: And if it is Rabbi Shimon,
let him follow the time of redemption,
and let them be redeemed along with their land,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the trees. At redemption time they are part of a consecrated field, so the field's price would cover them.

phrases.english: for we have heard regarding Rabbi Shimon
that he follows the time of redemption!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵיזִיל בָּתַר פִּדְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 3 by showing that the quoted clause clashes with רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא, including its last clause, follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון judges by the time of redemption. At that time both the trees and the land are הקדש, so the trees should be redeemed together with the land at the fixed price, not separately at their value.

steps.title: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון: consecrated first, father died later
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a son buys a field from his father, consecrates it, and then his father dies, the field is treated as a שדה אחוזה. This is the view of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: A man bought a field from his father and consecrated it, and only afterward his father died. How do we know the field counts for him as an inherited field? The פסוק says 'a field he bought, which is not of his inherited fields.' That means a field that could never have become his inherited field. This field is different, because it was fit to become his inherited field. These are the words of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for its claim that רבי שמעון goes by the time of redemption. This is the first piece of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment the son consecrated it, the field was only a bought field, because his father was still alive. Still, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say it counts as a שדה אחוזה. The ברייתא's stated reason is that the field was fit to come to him by inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: An inherited family field; its redemption rules differ from a bought field
A field someone bought, not inherited
'The פסוק teaches' – introduces the source
Fit or suitable (here: fit to come to him by inheritance)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the order of events. In this case the son consecrated the field while his father was still alive, and only afterward the father died.

phrases.english: As it is taught: From where do we know, regarding one who buys a field from his father
and consecrated it, and afterward his father died –
from where do we know that it is considered for him like an inherited field?
The verse teaches:
"And if a field he bought
which is not of his inherited fields" –

phrases.aramaic: שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵין רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה,
phrases.english: meaning a field that is not fit to become an inherited field,

phrases.aramaic: יָצְתָה זוֹ – שֶׁרְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה;
phrases.english: this one is excluded, since it is fit to become an inherited field;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for step 4's claim that רבי שמעון goes by the time of redemption.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון judges the status of consecrated property by the time of פדיון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a son who consecrated a field bought from his father before the father died.

steps.title: רבי מאיר uses the same פסוק for a different case
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads the same פסוק as teaching only the case where the father died first and the son consecrated the field afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: A man bought a field from his father, his father died, and afterward he consecrated it. How do we know it counts for him as an inherited field? The פסוק says 'a field he bought, which is not of his inherited fields.' That means a field that is not an inherited field right now. This one is excluded, because it already is an inherited field.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with רבי מאיר's view, which reads the same פסוק differently. This sets up the contrast the גמרא will use next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר looks at the field's status right now, when it is consecrated. If the father has already died, the field is inherited, so it counts as a שדה אחוזה. He does not apply the פסוק to a field that was only 'fit' to be inherited.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That it is', meaning it already is an inherited field, as opposed to 'fit to be'

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
From where do we know, regarding one who buys a field from his father,
and his father died, and afterward he consecrated it,
from where do we know that it is considered for him like an inherited field?
The verse teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאִם אֶת שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״ –
phrases.english: "And if a field he bought, which is not of his inherited fields" –
meaning a field that is not an inherited field,
this one is excluded, since it is an inherited field.
phrases.notes: Notice the change from step 5: there it said 'fit to be' an inherited field, here it says 'is' an inherited field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other opinion in the same ברייתא, reading the same פסוק for an easier case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the פסוק teaches that a field consecrated after the father's death counts as a שדה אחוזה.

steps.title: For רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the easy case needs no פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון need no פסוק when the father died first. They need the פסוק only for the case where the son consecrated first and the father died later.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון do not need a פסוק for the case where the father died first and then the son consecrated the field. They need the פסוק only for the case where he consecrated it first and then his father died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from comparing the two opinions. It shows that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון are saying something bigger than רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the father has already died, the field is plainly inherited at the time of consecration, so no פסוק is needed. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון go further. Even when the son consecrated the field before inheriting it, it still counts as inherited. That is the new point the גמרא is about to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whereas', introducing a contrast
They do not need a פסוק, because it is obvious
Was needed

phrases.english: Whereas Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּמֵת אָבִיו וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ –
phrases.english: where his father died and afterward he consecrated it –
they do not need a verse;
where the verse was needed –

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּהִקְדִּישָׁהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת אָבִיו.
phrases.english: is where he consecrated it and afterward his father died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two opinions in the ברייתא to show how far רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון go.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון count the field as inherited even though it was consecrated before the inheritance.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The comparison between the two readings of the פסוק in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Their real reason: they go by the time of redemption
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק by itself could be read like רבי מאיר. So רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון must have a reason of their own: they go by the time of פדיון, when the field is already inherited.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do they get this from? If only from this פסוק, you could say the פסוק comes to teach רבי מאיר's case! Rather, isn't it because they go by the time of redemption?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the real source is for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. It answers that they look at the time of redemption, and that completes the proof that רבי שמעון goes by פדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק alone does not force their reading, because it could just as easily teach רבי מאיר's simpler case. So their view must come from a principle: what counts is the field's status when it is redeemed. By that time the father has died and the field is inherited. This is exactly the claim from step 4, so it backs up the question there: by the time of redemption, the trees and the land are both הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where do they know it?', asking for the source
'I could say', offering another way to read it
'Rather, is it not...?', pointing to the only remaining explanation
They go by the time of redemption

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון (with רבי יהודה) judges consecrated property by its status at the time of פדיון. If so, the trees in step 4 should be redeemed together with the land. The next step rejects this suggestion.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof stood, it would back up step 4's question against saying that the ברייתא about trees and land follows רבי שמעון. Step 9 takes the proof apart.

phrases.english: From where do they know this?
If from this verse,
I could say it comes to teach like Rabbi Meir!
phrases.notes: Meaning the פסוק could be teaching only the easy case, where the father died first.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָזְלִי בָּתַר פִּדְיוֹן?
phrases.english: Rather, is it not because they follow the time of redemption?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the view described in step 7 and finishes the proof for step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון goes by the time of פדיון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק cannot force their reading, so their view must rest on the principle of following the time of redemption.

steps.title: Their ruling comes from a verse, not from the time of redemption
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that, generally, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון do not go by the time of פדיון. In this case they learned the rule from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק says: Really, in general, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון do not go by the time of redemption. But here, they found a verse and learned from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from earlier. It says רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון do not usually go by the time of פדיון, so the ברייתא about trees can still follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 assumed that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון rule this way because they look at the time of פדיון. If so, the trees should be redeemed together with the land, which was the challenge in Step 4. רב נחמן בר יצחק removes that assumption: their ruling about the son's field comes from a special reading of the פסוק, not from a general rule about פדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; used to hold on to an earlier position while explaining it differently
In general, in other cases
They go after / follow (a certain point in time)
They found a verse and expounded it

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer allows the ברייתא about consecrated trees to follow רבי שמעון after all, which closes the challenge from Step 4.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says:
Actually, in general,
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon
do not go by the time of redemption;
but here, they found a verse and expounded it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לְעוֹלָם בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning of Step 8 (that they go by the time of פדיון) and gives a different source for their ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different source for the opinion: a reading of the פסוק instead of a general principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון rule that the son's field is a שדה אחוזה because they go by the time of פדיון, so רבי שמעון cannot be the author of the trees ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their ruling comes from a reading of the פסוק. In general they do not go by the time of פדיון, so the trees ברייתא can follow רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Reading the extra wording of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have used simpler wording. The wording it does use, "אשר לא משדה אחוזתו", teaches that only a field that could never become a שדה אחוזה counts as a bought field.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verse should have written "And if a field he bought, which is not his ancestral holding", or else "his ancestral field". Why does it say "which is not of his ancestral field"? It means a field that is not fit to become an ancestral field. That leaves out this field, which is fit to become an ancestral field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly how רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read the פסוק. The unusual wording tells us that a field which could become inherited land is treated as a שדה אחוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only meant what רבי מאיר says, simpler wording would have been enough: either "אשר לא אחוזתו" or "שדה אחוזתו". The fuller phrase "מִשְּׂדֵה אחוזתו" points to a field that by its nature can never become a שדה אחוזה. A field a son bought from his father can become inherited land when the father dies, so it is left out of the "bought field" category, even if he consecrated it first.

keyTerms.meaning: A field that was bought (not inherited)
An inherited, ancestral family field
Fit / able to become
This one is excluded

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, a bought field that can later become inherited land (like a son's field bought from his father) is treated as a שדה אחוזה. They learn this from the wording of the פסוק, not from a rule about the time of פדיון.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write:
phrases.notes: "If so" means: if the פסוק only means what רבי מאיר says.

phrases.english: "And if a field that he bought
which is not his ancestral holding,"
or else: "his ancestral field."
What is meant by "which is not of his ancestral field"?
A field that is not fit
to be an ancestral field.
This one is excluded,
since it is fit to be an ancestral field.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the son's field bought from his father, which becomes inherited land once the father dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reading of the פסוק that Step 9 said רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון rely on.
steps.raayaObject: That a bought field which can become inherited land is treated as a שדה אחוזה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The unusual wording "אשר לא משדה אחוזתו" in ויקרא 27:22, where simpler wording would have been enough.

steps.title: A grafted carob and a sycamore trunk count as both a tree and land
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a חרוב המורכב and a סדן השקמה are treated as a tree in one way and as land in another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: A grafted carob and a sycamore trunk have the status of a tree and the status of land. They have the status of a tree: if someone consecrated or sold two trees plus this one, he has the land too. They have the status of land: they are not sold along with land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. רב הונא gives a ruling about two special trees and then explains both sides of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As a tree: it joins two other trees to make a group of three, and three trees bring the land between them along in a sale or הקדש. As land: these trees are so important that they act like a separate piece of land, so selling a field does not include them.

keyTerms.meaning: A grafted carob tree
The trunk of a sycamore tree that is cut back to grow new branches
The legal status of a tree
The legal status of land
Along with the land

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the trees are 'not really trees'. They are trees, and for one specific rule (being sold along with a field) they are treated like separate land.

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
A grafted carob and a sycamore trunk
have the status of a tree
and the status of land.
It has the status of a tree,
since where one consecrated or sold
two trees and this one,
he has land.
phrases.notes: Together they make three trees, and three trees bring the land between them along.

phrases.english: It has the status of land,
since it is not sold along with the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: חָרוּב הַמּוּרְכָּב וְסַדַּן הַשִּׁקְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the son's field ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A grafted carob and a sycamore trunk count as a tree when grouping three trees together, and as land in that they are not included when a field is sold.

steps.title: A sheaf of two סאה counts as a sheaf for counting
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a sheaf containing two סאה has the status of both a sheaf and a heap. As a sheaf, it counts as one of three sheaves, so the three are not שכחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא says: A sheaf with two סאה in it has the status of a sheaf and the status of a heap. It has the status of a sheaf: two forgotten sheaves are שכחה, but two plus this one are not שכחה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a second ruling of the same type, this time about a large sheaf and the laws of שכחה. This step explains the 'sheaf' side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of שכחה is that two forgotten sheaves must be left for the poor, but three forgotten together do not have to be. The large sheaf counts as an ordinary sheaf for this count, so two sheaves plus this one make three, and the owner may take them back.

keyTerms.meaning: A sheaf of harvested grain
Two סאה (a measure of volume), a very large sheaf
A heap or stack of grain
Forgotten sheaves that must be left for the poor

steps.confusionAlert: It is not the case that more forgotten sheaves means more for the poor. Two forgotten sheaves go to the poor, but three forgotten together do not.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna says:
A sheaf that contains two se'ah
has the status of a sheaf
and the status of a heap.
It has the status of a sheaf,
since two sheaves are a forgotten sheaf,
but two and this one are not a forgotten sheaf.
phrases.notes: With this big sheaf there are three sheaves, and three forgotten together don't have to be left for the poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: עוֹמֶר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ סָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling by רב הונא with the same 'two statuses' pattern as Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A two-סאה sheaf counts as one sheaf when counting forgotten sheaves, so two sheaves plus it are not שכחה.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה that the big sheaf counts as a heap
steps.stepSummary: The 'heap' side of the ruling is supported by a משנה in פאה: a forgotten sheaf of two סאה is not שכחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It has the status of a heap, as we learned in a משנה: A sheaf with two סאה in it that he forgot is not שכחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show the 'heap' side of רב הונא's ruling. Alone, this big sheaf is treated like a heap and is not left for the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A heap is too important to count as forgotten, so the laws of שכחה do not apply to it. The משנה says the same about a two-סאה sheaf, which shows it is treated like a heap when it is forgotten by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He forgot it

steps.whatToRemember: A two-סאה sheaf has two roles. When it is forgotten alone it acts like a heap and is not שכחה. When it is counted with other sheaves it is one sheaf, so two plus it make three and are not שכחה.

phrases.english: It has the status of a heap,
as we learned in a mishna:
A sheaf that contains two se'ah
that one forgot is not a forgotten sheaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's ruling from Step 12 by supporting its 'heap' side with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a two-סאה sheaf has the status of a heap.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה פאה 6:6: a forgotten sheaf of two סאה is not שכחה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש links the grafted carob and sycamore trunk to an existing dispute
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that whether a חרוב המורכב and a סדן השקמה become הקדש along with a field depends on the מחלוקת between רבי מנחם בר יוסי and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of ריש לקיש: about a grafted carob tree and a sycamore trunk, we have reached the argument between רבי מנחם בר יוסי and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from ריש לקיש. He says that the law of a חרוב המורכב and a סדן השקמה is not a brand-new question, because it matches an argument that already exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether these two items count as part of the field, so they become הקדש with it. ריש לקיש does not decide the answer himself. He says that רבי מנחם בר יוסי holds they are not made הקדש with the field, while the רבנן hold that they are.

keyTerms.meaning: "We have reached the argument": this question depends on an argument that already exists
The majority of the sages, who disagree with him

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not giving his own ruling here. He is only saying that the answer depends on which side of the מחלוקת you follow.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Reish Lakish said:
A grafted carob tree and a sycamore trunk:
we have reached the dispute
of Rabbi Menaḥem bar Yosei and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: באנו למחלוקת רבי מנחם בר יוסי ורבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the same two items from רב הונא's ruling in Step 11 and brings a new statement about them, this time about making a field הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether a חרוב המורכב and a סדן השקמה become הקדש with a field depends on the מחלוקת between רבי מנחם בר יוסי, who says they do not, and the רבנן, who say they do.
